newsitem.title: USA: U.S. blue chips push higher as techs shine.
newsitem.headline: U.S. blue chips push higher as techs shine.

text.p: U.S. blue chips moved off early lows to trade barely changed at midday Tuesday, while surging technology stocks took center stage once again.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average was mired in negative territory for most of the morning, unable to shake weakness in the bond market. But around midday it pushed higher and was down just six points at 8192.
While the Dow traded near unchanged levels, investors shifted their focus to the buoyant technology sector. The Nasdaq composite gained 12 points to 1618.

"Money is going into technology," said Roy Blumberg, chief investment strategist at Josephthal Lyon & Ross. "Dow stocks have been languishing because techs stocks are warming the cockles of everybody's heart."

Tech stocks, which lent support to the broader stock market on Monday in the face of bond market declines, again assumed market leadership. Shares of semiconductor and semiconductor equipment makers powered higher.
Market heavyweight Intel Corp jumped 2-15/16 to 99-11/16 and Microsoft Corp rose 2-2/16 to 143-11/16.
As money poured into the sector, shares of Dow components Hewlett-Packard Co and International Business Machines Corp also rose.
"The performance of the technology is mind-boggling," said Dick Stein, vice president of U.S. Clearing Corp. "They continue to plough ahead."
Blumberg said, "It's the usual suspects -- Intel and Microsoft...When there is heat in a certain area, the money comes in. Money is chasing money in this market."
The Dow's advance was hampered by investors' rotating funds and by a sluggish bond market, analysts said.

The long bond was down 6/32 to yield 6.49 percent. Its yields have been climbing on renewed concerns about higher interest rates and inflation. Today it also braced for the Treasury's $16 billion three-year note auction.
Analysts said blue chips shared some of bonds' concerns about higher rates because their valuations were lofty.

"The stock market is very sensitive to the bond market at these levels," said Henry Herrmann, chief investment officer, Waddell & Reed. "It is in a holding pattern, crunching through numbers to see how much the economy is reaccelerating."

Among particular issues, Lone Star Steakhouse & Saloon Inc tumbled about 20 percent in brisk trade after the company said its third quarter profits would not meet analysts' expectations. The stock fell 4-1/8 to 17-7/8.
Shares of Aetna Inc and other health maintenance organizations slipped after Aetna's U.S. Healthcare unit posted disappointing second quarter earnings.
Aetna shed 12-7/8 to 104-1/8, Oxford Health Plans fell 3-29/64 to 81-29/64, and United HealthCare Corp lost 1-5/8 to 58-1/8.
